nodes.title: A question of Erdős and Graham on covering systems

nodes.summary: A covering system of a commutative semiring $R$ is a finite family of cosets $r_i + I_i = \{r_i + a : a \in I_i\}$, where each $I_i$ is an ideal of $R$ different from both $\{0\}$ and $R$, whose union is all of $R$. In the case $R = \mathbb{Z}$, this corresponds to a choice of finitely many congruences $x \equiv r_i \pmod{n_i}$ with moduli $n_i \ge 2$ such that every integer satisfies at least one of them.
nodes.title: Covering system

nodes.summary: A covering system of a commutative semiring $R$, given by cosets $r_i + I_i$, is strict if the ideals $I_i$ are pairwise distinct. In the case $R = \mathbb{Z}$, this means that the congruences defining it have pairwise distinct moduli.
